_comment: Scenario-staged routing-around-terrain demo: a brittle player cavalry unit (60 mounts at morale 3) HOLDS just west of the impassable hill; an enemy cavalry charge from its WESTERN flank breaks it on contact. The player no longer auto-advances, so the spawn sits west of the hill's west face (x=1100, hill from x=1150) -- a hold at the old (1250, 620) south-of-hill spot lets the charge herd the router south-east, off the flee lane, and the clip never shows the detour. From this west-of-hill hold the northward flee runs along the west face at the unit's own clearance margin -- the same routing an ordered march gets -- while the recovering pursuer traces the same corridor and runs it down at the northwest shoulder. The flank angle is still load-bearing: a charge from dead behind overshoots NORTH onto the flee lane and physically walls it, a contact pursuer that stays on the lane herds and grinds the mob, and archer fire pins it prone into a crawl. This scenario does NOT demonstrate the separate 'stands and fights when genuinely trapped' behavior -- the hill is a single free-standing obstacle nowhere near a field edge; that case is covered by test_trapped_routing_unit_fights_instead_of_fleeing. No player input needed; the scenario + seed make the clash deterministic. Sampled ticks pin the router's story beats (hold at spawn, break, climb the west face, the catch at the far shoulder): the pursuer's own formation progressively deforms during the long gallop chase -- a known, separately tracked sim question -- so mid-gallop samples of the pursuer's cosmetics are deliberately not part of this clip's declared checks.
